places.name: Nairobi
places.context: Nairobi is Kenya's commercial capital, where distributors, retailers and corporate buyers sit within a few kilometres of each other — and where suppliers are judged on response time and follow-through.

places.name: Mombasa
places.context: Mombasa's port and tourism economy means supply chains and premises that cannot afford downtime, with buyers who work across the island, the mainland and the coastal strip.

places.name: Kisumu
places.context: Kisumu is the Lake Victoria trading hub for western Kenya, connecting county distributors, lake-side logistics and a fast-growing retail and services market.

places.name: Nakuru
places.context: Nakuru anchors the Rift Valley corridor between Nairobi and western Kenya, with a dense mix of agricultural processors, wholesalers and highway-facing retail.

places.name: Eldoret
places.context: Eldoret is one of Kenya's fastest-growing towns, with a strong agri-processing base, a university economy and growing demand for professional services delivered locally rather than from Nairobi.

localAngles.cctv-surveillance-systems/nairobi: Nairobi CCTV jobs are rarely about camera count: upstairs offices need cable routes that survive a landlord's renovation, and shops along Thika Road need footage that still identifies a face at night.
localAngles.cctv-surveillance-systems/mombasa: Mombasa installations have to survive salt air and monsoon power dips — marine-grade housings, surge protection and a recorder that restarts clean after an outage matter more than megapixels.
localAngles.cctv-surveillance-systems/kisumu: In Kisumu we usually start at the lake-facing yard and the loading gate: the two places where stock leaves quietly, and where one camera pointing the wrong way sinks the whole project.
localAngles.cctv-surveillance-systems/nakuru: Nakuru sites often stretch between the CBD and a highway yard, so we plan point-to-point wireless links instead of assuming one recorder can reach both.
localAngles.cctv-surveillance-systems/eldoret: Eldoret work is mostly agri-processors and campus-adjacent businesses, where dust, long cable runs and a maintenance visit that does not need a Nairobi flight set the design.
localAngles.fmcg-order-booking/nairobi: Nairobi order books are built around traffic: call cycles are grouped by corridor so a rep spends the day selling in Industrial Area rather than sitting on Mombasa Road.
localAngles.fmcg-order-booking/mombasa: On the coast the call cycle follows the stock, not the clock — island outlets in the morning, Nyali and Bamburi in the afternoon, with depot cut-offs that respect port clearance days.
localAngles.fmcg-order-booking/kisumu: Kisumu bookings usually span the lake ring and the county towns inland, so the order form has to handle routes that take a full day and depots that only load twice a week.
localAngles.fmcg-order-booking/nakuru: Nakuru is a highway market: bookings are planned around Naivasha and Gilgil runs, and confirmation calls happen before the trucks leave rather than after.
localAngles.fmcg-order-booking/eldoret: Eldoret order capture is seasonal — planting, harvest and school terms move volume fast — so call cycles and credit limits have to flex with the agricultural calendar.
localAngles.fmcg-sales/nairobi: Nairobi's fight is for shelf space in modern trade alongside the dukas that still move the volume; coverage and pack architecture have to be planned for both at once.
localAngles.fmcg-sales/mombasa: Mombasa distribution splits between the island, the mainland and the tourist strip, and trade terms have to reflect three very different logistics realities.
localAngles.fmcg-sales/kisumu: In Kisumu the distributor network reaches well beyond the city into Siaya, Vihiga and Homa Bay, so territory design has to account for routes that cross counties.
localAngles.fmcg-sales/nakuru: Nakuru rewards route discipline: the town is a staging point for Rift Valley trade, and reps who cover the highway towns consistently are the ones who win the volume.
localAngles.fmcg-sales/eldoret: Eldoret's market is agricultural and institutional — agri-inputs, processors and campuses — so the sales plan is built around buying seasons rather than monthly pushes.
localAngles.fmcg-supplier-sourcing/nairobi: Nairobi sourcing conversations end at landed cost: we benchmark against Industrial Area wholesalers and the import route through Mombasa before recommending anyone.
localAngles.fmcg-supplier-sourcing/mombasa: Mombasa is where the container actually lands, so supplier vetting includes clearing timelines, port charges and who carries demurrage when a shipment slips.
localAngles.fmcg-supplier-sourcing/kisumu: Kisumu sourcing leans on lake and cross-border supply, so we check quality consistency and restocking cadence rather than just the first quote.
localAngles.fmcg-supplier-sourcing/nakuru: Nakuru suppliers are often processors close to the farm — good prices, volatile capacity — and we qualify both before you commit volume.
localAngles.fmcg-supplier-sourcing/eldoret: Eldoret gives access to grain, dairy and agri-input suppliers; the work is proving capacity through a harvest cycle, not a single sample.

fmcg-order-booking.angle: A national order book only works when the desk in Nairobi and the rep in Kisumu agree on the same price, the same MOQ and the same credit position. Kenyan FMCG orders usually flow through depots in Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru and Eldoret, with distributors covering the counties in between. We run one order form, one confirmation script and one daily reconciliation across all of them, so a booking taken on the coast is visible to the depot that has to load it the same afternoon.
fmcg-order-booking.model: National order booking is run as five depot clusters feeding one central desk: reps capture orders on a fixed call cycle, the desk confirms stock, MOQ and credit, then releases a dispatch list to the nearest depot per route.

fmcg-sales.angle: Kenya is not one market. Modern trade in Nairobi and Mombasa behaves differently from the dukas and kiosks that still carry most FMCG volume, and both behave differently from distributor-led trade in the counties. A national sales plan has to set separate coverage standards, pack sizes and trade terms for each channel, then hold one reporting standard across all of them. That is the work: route design, distributor terms and rep routines that survive contact with a real market.
fmcg-sales.model: National sales programmes are built channel by channel — modern trade, traditional trade and distributor-led county coverage — with territory targets, pricing architecture and a monthly sell-in/sell-out review that the whole country reports into.

fmcg-supplier-sourcing.angle: Nationally, sourcing is a landed-cost question. Mombasa handles the containers, Nairobi's Industrial Area and Thika hold the manufacturers and importers, and Nakuru, Eldoret and Kisumu sit close to the processors and farms. Vetting a supplier across that spread means checking clearing timelines and port charges on the coast, capacity through a harvest upcountry, and quality consistency between batches — not simply comparing a price list.
fmcg-supplier-sourcing.model: National sourcing runs as a shortlist, sample and audit cycle: landed cost is benchmarked for imported lines, capacity is tested through a peak season for local lines, and onboarding is batched by region so travel does not inflate the cost of diligence.

fmcg-merchandizing.angle: Shelf standards are national until they meet a specific store. A Nairobi supermarket planogram has to survive a smaller Mombasa outlet with different fixtures, and a Kisumu kiosk needs a different visibility answer again. We set the standard centrally, then train merchandiser pods per city to execute it with photo evidence, so the report shows what is actually on shelf rather than what was planned in the office.
fmcg-merchandizing.model: Merchandising runs in city pods — Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru and Eldoret — with a shared planogram library, weekly photo audits and a national compliance summary for the brand owner.

fmcg-product-promotion.angle: Promotion timing across Kenya follows money and calendar, not a brand's internal quarter. Paydays, school terms, planting and harvest, Ramadan and December trade all move volume in different counties at different times. A national promotion calendar has to stagger activations around those windows and measure lift per outlet, or the spend simply discounts sales that would have happened anyway.
fmcg-product-promotion.model: National promotions are planned on one calendar, then activated city by city with outlet-level redemption tracking, so lift is measured against a control group rather than assumed from volume.

strategic-business-planning.angle: A national plan is mostly a set of choices about where not to compete. Kenyan businesses often want to be in Nairobi, the coast and the lake region at once; the plan has to say which market funds the next one, which costs are fixed versus route-dependent, and what has to be true before a second county is opened. We work from your actual numbers — margin by line, cost to serve by route — rather than a template deck.
strategic-business-planning.model: Planning engagements run remotely with working sessions, plus in-person workshops in Nairobi when the board needs them, and produce a written plan with numbers, owners and review dates.

cctv-surveillance-systems.angle: Nationwide CCTV is a logistics problem as much as an installation one. Equipment has to reach a site in Kilifi or Kisumu in the same condition it left Nairobi, installers on the ground need the same commissioning checklist, and someone has to own the maintenance call three months later. We design centrally, install through vetted local teams, and keep one record of every camera, cable run and warranty across the country.
cctv-surveillance-systems.model: National rollouts use a standard site survey, a single equipment specification and local installation partners, with remote health checks and a maintenance rota agreed per region before the first drill goes in.

ai-system-integration.angle: Kenyan AI projects live or die on the boring parts: where the data sits, who is allowed to see it, whether the system can take M-Pesa and whether staff will use it on a phone rather than a laptop. Integration work here has to respect the Data Protection Act, work over patchy connectivity, and hand over documentation a local IT person can actually maintain after we leave.
ai-system-integration.model: National AI integration is delivered remotely with a Nairobi kick-off where needed: data mapping, a small pilot on one workflow, documented handover and a support window before anything is called live.

custom-corporate-websites.angle: For most Kenyan organisations the website is the first credibility check a buyer makes, often on a phone and on mobile data. That changes the brief: light pages, fast first paint, clear contact routes, M-Pesa or bank details where payment matters, and content a non-technical administrator can update. County governments, SACCOs, schools and agri-businesses each need a different structure for the same underlying standard.
custom-corporate-websites.model: National website work is delivered remotely: discovery calls, a staging link you can review, content and admin training over video, then launch and a support window. On-site sessions in Nairobi are available when a team needs them.

marketplace-listings.angle: Selling on Jumia or Kilimall nationally is a catalogue and fulfilment discipline, not a listing. Titles, images, categories and pricing rules decide whether a product is found; stock accuracy and delivery promises decide whether it stays live. We build the listing structure, the pricing and promotion rules, and the reconciliation between marketplace orders and your own stock so oversells stop.
marketplace-listings.model: Marketplace work runs remotely with a catalogue build, feed and pricing rules, then weekly reconciliation against stock and a review of returns and cancellation reasons by county.

account-social-media-management.angle: A national social presence in Kenya is really several local conversations. Nairobi audiences argue about convenience and price, the coast responds to tourism seasonality, and county audiences engage heavily through WhatsApp groups and Facebook rather than the platforms a brand team uses daily. We run one brand voice with a local content calendar, English and Swahili where it is natural, and community replies handled within a working day.
account-social-media-management.model: Social management is remote with a monthly content calendar, platform-specific formats, a WhatsApp channel where it fits the audience, and a monthly report on reach, replies and enquiries by region.

ad-generation.angle: Nationally, paid media is wasted when it targets 'Kenya' as one audience. Cost per enquiry differs sharply between Nairobi, the coast and the lake region, and a campaign that works for a Nairobi service business can fail for an upcountry retailer. We build creative per audience, geo-target by county, and judge spend on qualified enquiries rather than impressions or likes.
ad-generation.model: Ad programmes run remotely: audience and offer research, creative sets per region, Meta and Google campaigns, and a weekly report on spend, cost per qualified enquiry and the counties producing them.
